countMethod: 36 explicitly logged correction groups from docs/audit-system-design.json, not a sentence-level factual assertion count. Completed full semantic read of all 8 lessons and all 96 question records.
corrections: A five-node majority needs leader plus two of four followers.
Official ZooKeeper internals contradicts unconditional sync guarantee.
Complexity depends on number of differing subtrees, not universally logarithmic.
Original incorrectly called reverse causal ordering concurrent.
HLC encoding is not universally 64 bits; Cockroach uses wall time plus logical component.
Avoid implying every named implementation uses 48+16 encoding.
Replication does not eliminate 2PC blocking under partitions.
Reusing an API idempotency key for different actions can replay wrong result or be rejected.
Sagas also give up global atomicity, as correctly stated earlier.
Phi is not posterior probability of a detection mistake; it is a tail probability under the observed heartbeat model.
Universal impossibility contradicts bounded-counter example; invariant preservation depends on operations.
Qualify overbroad invariant claim.
Replication reduces single-node blocking, not partitions.
Cassandra uses mean-based exponential detector; original normal-distribution example and false-positive interpretation were wrong.
Align lesson with actual Cassandra detector.
Idempotency alone does not preserve order of different ledger transactions during consumer overlap.
Partition assignment does not fence writes to external systems.
Highest-seen-token fencing is conditional on resource observing newer epoch.
Unqualified takeaway omitted sticky-availability assumption.
Timed pinning cannot guarantee read-your-writes under unbounded lag.
Sticky replica alone does not handle rollback or failover.
Concurrent writes may be linearised in either order; timed-out write visibility alone is allowed.
Failure response type matters; unknown outcome visibility not itself violation.
Causal partition availability needs sticky-client qualification.
Version requirement through failover is not optional for the claimed guarantee.
Eventual convergence is a liveness condition, not another step in this safety implication chain. Session guarantees are not all equivalent to PRAM.
Explain safety versus liveness instead of claiming total hierarchy.
3PC recovery needs termination protocol, not local phase-only timeout decisions.
Replace incorrect local timeout rules with termination-protocol explanation.
Clarify operation correlation versus shared API idempotency key.
Write quorum overlap is not mutual exclusion.
Larger quorum is not proof wall-clock commits always slower.
Quorum order statistic determines latency.
etcd comparison cannot fence arbitrary external writes; make shared transaction scope explicit.
Concurrent writes lack inherent causal winner.
3PC requires termination state exchange not simplistic local timeout decisions.
